subject: Rackless VPC cluster readiness – node pools, NICs & storage preflight

Subject: Rackless VPC cluster readiness – node pools, NICs & storage preflight

Alex —

Thanks for the intake notes you shared in the portal. Before we schedule the onsite/network call with EdgeHosting, a quick preflight to align expectations will help avoid a costly rework. Attached is a short checklist and a nodepool YAML template we usually validate against during our engineering intake. Key areas we want to confirm:

- Cluster footprint: control plane placement (hosted vs customer VPC), expected node counts for prod/staging, and autoscaling guards.
- Networking: service CIDR, pod CIDR, whether BGP sessions terminate in the VPC, and any NAT/eBPF egress constraints.
- Storage: NVMe local vs blockstore (iSCSI/Ceph), encryption at rest approach (KMS/HSM), and whether you need writable local volumes for model caches.
- Ops: log/audit retention, kube-audit sink, and where snapshots land (S3-compatible bucket?).

Quick ask: please confirm the inventory sheet (I attached a blank copy) with the actual subnet sizes and whether you have a managed NAT gateway or on-prem NAT. If you can reply with those details today/tomorrow, Neha and Karthik will propose the node-pool sizing and CSI driver choices.

Attachments: rackless_preflight_checklist.pdf, nodepool_template.yaml, northpoint-site-inventory.xlsx

Next steps: I’ll propose two 45-min windows for a technical sync after we receive the inventory.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lauren —

Thanks, appreciate the checklist. I filled the inventory (attached) and answered a few inline questions below. High level: we want the control plane in our VPC (customer-managed control plane), no co-located racks at our site — we expect a rackless topology where hosts are provisioned by EdgeHosting in our subnet ranges. A couple of clarified points:

- Subnets: we have three /22s available (one for control-plane LB + API, one for node pools, one reserved for on-prem peering).
- BGP: yes — we terminate BGP at the VPC edge and have a transit gateway that peers to our on-prem fabric.
- NAT/Egress: we have a managed NAT gateway for outbound egress, but some regulated services require egress via our on-prem NAT for auditing.
- Storage: we'd prefer encrypted NVMe local for model cache (we plan to encrypt with LUKS, key material managed in our KMS), and Ceph/RBD for durable blockstore.
- Runtimes: containerd 1.6.18, kubelet flags: --eviction-hard=imagefs.available<5%,nodefs.available<10% (we can adjust), and we plan to use GKE-style node auto-repair via the host provider.

I attached the completed northpoint-site-inventory.xlsx and a short note from our infra_ops alias about expected sustained pod density (avg 45 pods/node for medium nodes).

Questions for Redwood:
1) Does Redwood require a control-plane private endpoint inside the VPC (we prefer that) or is a managed control plane with private connectivity OK?
2) For local NVMe volumes encrypted with LUKS, do you support preserving the device mapper/volume across node replacements or should we plan for cache rehydration on restart?

Alex Douglass
Director, Infrastructure — Northpoint Health Systems
alex.douglass@northpoint.com | +1 (212) 555-8891

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Douglass <alex.douglass@northpoint.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 07:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rackless VPC cluster readiness – node pools, NICs & storage preflight

Alex / team —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the inventory sheet — helpful. Short answers up front, then recommended config based on what you shared.

1) Control plane: We can run a customer-managed control plane inside the VPC (recommended for data residency & VPC-native routing). Redwood will deploy the control plane components into your control-plane subnet and expose a private API endpoint behind an internal LB. This gives full routing control and avoids egress to public endpoints.

2) LUKS + local NVMe: Local NVMe encrypted with LUKS is fine for model cache. Note: node replacement will destroy local device contents by default. If you need cache persistence across node replacement, we recommend either: (a) attach a small network-backed blockstore (RBD or cloud-block) for persistent cache, or (b) use a shared cache layer (NFS/MinIO edge) with local warmers. For model correctness we assume cache rehydration is acceptable (we typically design for graceful cold start).

Recommended baseline (based on ~45 pods/node):
- K8s: 1.26.x (we validate on 1.26/1.27), containerd 1.6.x — kubelet eviction thresholds conservatively set to imagefs.available<6%,nodefs.available<12% for safer headroom.
- Node classes:
  * control-plane (3 x m5.large-equivalent VMs in control subnet; internal LB with health checks)
  * compute-medium (autoscaling pool: min 6 / desired 12 / max 40; 32Gi RAM, 8 vCPU, local NVMe 1TB for cache)
  * compute-large (for heavy-inference jobs: min 2 / desired 4 / max 12; 256Gi RAM with GPU attachment via PCI passthrough where required)
- CSI/Storage: Ceph/RBD for durable PVs; use csi-rbd for block volumes. For local NVMe caches use local-path-provisioner or local-static-provisioner with NodeFeatureDiscovery to advertise NVMe devices; ensure the CSI topology labels are set so workloads land on NVMe-capable nodes.
- Encryption & KMS: Integrate with your KMS over the private peering; Redwood's control plane can use customer KMS via our keywrap design (we do not persist raw keys).
- Networking: Use Cilium as CNI for eBPF acceleration and policy enforcement (better for high pod density and egress shaping). Service CIDR suggestion: 10.96.0.0/16 (can shrink if you prefer); Pod CIDR suggestion: 10.100.0.0/14 to avoid overlap with existing on-prem ranges. We recommend reserving /24s per nodepool for host-level predictable IPs when using host-based firewalls.
- Egress: Configure policy-based routing — control-plane traffic via internal LB, data egress can be routed through your managed NAT gateway; for audited flows we will add a route to on-prem NAT using the transit gateway VPN/BGP.
- Observability: ship kube-audit to your S3-compatible bucket; set retention 90 days by default, increase per compliance needs. Use node-exporter + Prometheus remote write to your monitoring endpoint.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a canary pool (small pool with same node image) to validate kernel modules and NVMe drivers before scaling.
- Patching: enable Node auto-repair and planned drains via cordon/drain with preStop hooks. For local-device durability, ensure the drain scripts either migrate state or mark caches for rehydrate.

Next actions we propose:
A) Redwood to produce a topology diagram and a concrete nodepool.yaml (we will use the attached template) — ETA EOD Wed 21 Oct.
B) Joint technical call with EdgeHosting and your infra_ops — propose Thu 22 Oct, 9:00am PT.
C) Confirm whether persistent cache is required across node replacement — Alex to confirm.

If that plan works, we’ll assemble an operational runbook and update the preflight checklist with exact CIDR mappings.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Infrastructure Architect, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Alex —

This looks great, thanks for the quick answers. Confirming the plan from our side and locking the proposed next actions:

- Redwood will deliver: topology diagram + populated nodepool_template.yaml with the compute-medium/large pools and the canary pool variations by EOD Wed 21 Oct. (attachment will be the filled nodepool_template.yaml)
- Joint technical sync: Thu 22 Oct, 09:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite and include EdgeHosting.
- Action item: Alex — confirm persistence requirement for local NVMe (yes/no). If yes, we’ll design a small RBD-backed cache layer.

Temporary decision points to capture in the runbook:
- Control plane: customer-managed inside the VPC (private API endpoint)
- CNI: Cilium (eBPF)
- Durable volumes: Ceph/RBD; local NVMe for ephemeral caches unless persistence requested
- Audit/log sink: northpoint S3-compatible bucket (we will request write credentials via the secure channel)

If there are any missing owners on the Northpoint side I should loop in, please let me know. Otherwise I’ll circulate the invite and share the populated templates tomorrow.

Thanks everyone —
Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
